architecture.mechanism: Colloidal monolayer membranes (CMMs) formed by anisotropic particles increase bending rigidity, enabling uniform deposition during evaporation and reducing edge accumulation.
architecture.intervention: Embed anisotropic, erosion-resistant nanoparticles (e.g., ellipsoidal silica or ceramic particles) into the leading-edge composite blade surface layer. The particles form a CMM during rain/hail impact, increasing surface rigidity and redistributing erosion forces uniformly across the blade edge rather than concentrating at the leading edge.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced localized erosion at the leading edge, minimizing material loss and extending time between scheduled repairs, thereby recovering 4-6% annual energy production loss.
architecture.falsification_test: Compare erosion rates of blade sections infused with ellipsoidal vs. spherical nanoparticles after controlled rain/hail exposure in a certified test chamber. Measure depth profiles of material loss along the leading edge; uniform erosion across the edge for ellipsoidal particles would validate the mechanism.
